discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of time-reversal-invariant topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 band topology)
subfield: Condensed matter physics: topological electronic states of matter
motivation: Kane and Mele (2005) showed that spin-orbit coupling can produce a quantum spin Hall state in time-reversal-invariant insulators. They introduced the Z2 topological invariant, which distinguishes ordinary insulators from topological ones that carry protected helical edge states. Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental proof in 2007. In HgTe/CdTe quantum wells they observed quantised edge conductance once the band inversion occurred. This confirmed that topology, and not only symmetry breaking, classifies phases of matter in real materials. The work extended topological band theory from quantum Hall systems in strong magnetic fields to ordinary crystals. It led to three-dimensional topological insulators such as Bi2Se3, to the quantum anomalous Hall effect, to Dirac and Weyl semimetals, and to systematic topological materials databases. Today it shapes spintronics, the search for Majorana modes, and photonic and other topological systems. This chain from concept to prediction to experiment deserves the Nobel Prize.
